claims.excerpt: How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Mass
claims.label: F0

claims.excerpt: GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: Twin satellites follow each other about 137 miles or 220 kilometers apart.
claims.synthesisStatement: The synthesis gives the same satellite count and approximate separation.
claims.narrativeStatement: The narrative’s context gives the same satellite count and separation.

claims.excerpt: Their changing separation is the measurement at the center of the mission: as gravity acts on the pair, the distance between them shifts.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The changing inter-satellite distance is a raw measurement used to infer shifts in mass. As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, stronger gravity acts on the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing one.
claims.synthesisStatement: The synthesis identifies changing separation as the raw measurement and explains the gravity-driven change.
claims.narrativeStatement: The narrative describes separation as the central measurement and says it changes as gravity acts on the pair.
claims.explanation: This accurately states the measurement’s central role and that gravity changes the spacing; the following sentence supplies the sequence and direction.
